properties.Location: South Side of Santa Rosa Island, Between Ford Point and South Point
properties.IncidentOverview: Current Situation – May 20th; 2026 Today; containment grew again; this time on the northern edge of the fire. Containment is now up to 44%. This evening firefighters reported minimal smoke visible from the park housing. Crews continued to strengthen Telephone Road on the northeastern edge of the fire; out to the coast; and monitoring the line for any new heat. Another crew was sent to Soledad Peak to conduct tactical firing operations; back burning to the south of Soledad Peak is being used as an indirect containment strategy to get ahead of the northwestern edge of the fire and reduce the fire’s intensity. Water scooping planes were used to do light water drops on some higher elevation ridge lines; often referred to as the Cloud Forest; and also used around Telephone Road to cool fuels ahead of the fire. In the last two days; scoopers have dropped 100;800 gallons of sea water on Santa Rosa Island. Based on initial assessments by firefighters and the flight imagery from an Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) module today; the Torrey Pines on Santa Rosa Island still exist and remain largely intact. The fire front came from south to north; and appears to have lost energy after burning through the non-native grasses downslope of the trees. By the time it reached the ridge along Upper Torrey Pines Road it transitioned into a backing fire with lower intensity and moved downhill towards the ocean. This type of fire tends to consume the understory vegetation and leaves the canopy largely intact. It appears that some small pockets of the Torrey Pines did burn with higher intensity within the larger stand. These pockets that sustained more damage were likely burned in short; uphill runs by the fire. This is typically caused by material like logs rolling down hill and carrying flame down; where it then burns up the slope with more vigor. This type of activity is common in areas with steep and rugged terrain like Santa Rosa Island. The National Park Service has special firefighters; known as fire effects crews that will go to this area taking measurements such as specific fire severity calculations and observations. This is not just a single snapshot but will be part of long-term monitoring of effects to better understand fire in this ecosystem. This long-term monitoring of fire effects will tie-in to Channel Islands National Park’s Inventory and Monitoring Program. Channel Islands National Park is the National Park Service’s first Prototype Park; leading the way in understanding and protecting the extraordinary terrestrial and marine ecosystems therein. Its pioneering approach provides essential scientific data that guides conservation of the park’s globally unique species and habitats; ensuring their protection for future generations. Tomorrow; firefighters working on the eastern half of the fire will focus on the cloud Forest along the Main (Soledad) Road working south towards the South Point Spur and the South Point Lighthouse. On the western side of the fire; crews will work from Soledad Peak eastward along Main (Soledad) Road along the contained fireline to ensure that line is still holding; and build more containment line along Telephone Road and Cherry Canyon. Background: On Friday; May 15; 2026; an aircraft flying over Santa Rosa Island in Channel Islands National Park reported a wildfire. National Park Service (NPS) staff already on the island confirmed it later that morning. The Santa Rosa Island Fire is located on the southeastern end of the island in remote and rugged terrain. This is a full-suppression human-caused wildfire and is under investigation. Closures: The National Park Service has closed Santa Rosa Island to day use and overnight use at least through this week due to the wildfire. Visitors with campground reservations at Water Canyon Campground have been notified via e-mail. Structures: There are two uninhabited historic structures in the area; Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed on the western edge; and Wreck Line Camp Cabin on the eastern edge. Unfortunately; both have been confirmed destroyed. An additional storage structure was also destroyed adjacent to Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed.
